clue.text: Backing provided by idiot, one with attitude

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot
I is the Roman numeral for one
a stance is a position or attitude taken on something

explanation.surface: Support offered by a fool who has a certain attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing someone means giving them support or help, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Two degrees from south and north, group of four stars?

indicators.note: read upwards from the bottom or downwards from the top the letters are the same, so this down entry is a palindrome

parts.note: AB and BA are both Bachelor of Arts degrees (AB the American form)

explanation.surface: Astronomical directions for finding a cluster of four stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two degrees' gives AB and BA; 'from south and north' tells you the result reads the same in either direction in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish pop group had four members, all stars, hence a quartet of stars; the question mark flags the pun on celestial stars.

clue.text: Speed aboard steamer, cool long-distance vessel

indicators.note: something aboard a ship is inside it, so one word goes within the steamer

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
pace means speed or rate
hip means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: A description of a fast, trendy ship built for long voyages.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft for travelling through space covers enormous distances, so it is a long-distance vessel.

clue.text: Drop off bits of fruit to be served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: peels are the skins, or bits, of fruit

explanation.surface: Instructions to let pieces of fruit fall before bringing them to the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is the idiom for falling asleep, so it matches the verb for slumbering.

clue.text: Set out and managed to puncture changing gear

indicators.note: a word that punctures another goes into the middle of it
changing tells us the letters of gear are to be altered in order

parts.note: ran as in ran a business, managed it

explanation.surface: Someone sets off and manages to get a gear-change job done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges the gear letters to ARGE, and 'to puncture' sends the managing word into the middle of that.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out things is to lay them in order, a synonym for arranging them.

clue.text: Observe telecom men taunting bears

indicators.note: the phrase bears, or carries, the word within its letters

explanation.surface: Watch phone engineers tease some bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals in the surface but signals that the letters are carried inside 'telecom men'.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe can mean to remark or say, which is to make a remark of this kind.

clue.text: One may deck in a ring or be decked in a ring

definitions.text: One may deck in a ring or be decked in a ring

parts.words: One may deck in a ring or be decked in a ring
parts.note: a boxer's clenched hand knocks an opponent down in the boxing ring, and the same hand may be adorned with a finger ring

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that floors people in the ring or wears jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'deck' (knock down, adorn) and 'ring' (boxing arena, piece of jewellery) are used in two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A clenched hand punches in boxing and can also wear a finger ring, fitting both readings.

clue.text: Country region of UK's taken up rising relief

indicators.note: in a down light, taken up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, a region of the United Kingdom

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters climb, so they read backwards

parts.note: aid is help or relief

explanation.surface: A part of Britain lifted by aid that is increasing.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Asian republic is a nation, so a plain example of a country.

clue.text: Neater flowing in the delta was imminent

indicators.note: one word sits in the other, inside the letters for the delta

parts.note: D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: flowing suggests movement, so the letters of neater are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something tidier was coming down the river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' gives REATEN from the tidier word, and 'in' places it after the first two letters of the opening piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that looms, as in rain loomed, is about to happen, so it was imminent.

clue.text: Reportedly stop work and slow down

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to break is to pause or stop work

explanation.surface: Supposedly people downed tools and eased off.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply the car's stopping mechanism is to slow down, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Dreamer writhing around in rest

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap round the other word
writhing means twisting about, so the letters of dreamer are mixed up

explanation.surface: A restless sleeper twisting and turning while trying to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhing' scrambles the sleeper to REMADER, and 'around' means those letters wrap round the small word from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest of something is what is left over, a synonym for the leftover part.

clue.text: Popular party's welcoming or not the place for outsiders?

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: do is a party, and with the s it gives dos

explanation.surface: A popular party lets guests in, or perhaps it is no venue for strangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside a building is literally the opposite of outside, so it is no spot for those outside; the question mark covers the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Get rid of old lover with little witticism and say that's over

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a pun is a small play on words

indicators.note: over signals turning the abbreviation backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, is a word for say

explanation.surface: Dump a former partner with a quip and declare it finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase or delete something entirely is to get rid of it.

clue.text: A parent attracted to doctor in interesting spectacles?

indicators.note: attracted to means drawn up next to, so these letters come after the doctor

parts.note: ma is mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A parent falls for a doctor wearing striking glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' pretends to mean glasses; here it means shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A play or theatrical show is a spectacle, and an exciting one at that; the question mark marks the glasses pun.

clue.text: Bits of text that often come in at the beginning

definitions.text: Bits of text that often come in at the beginning

parts.words: Bits of text that often come in at the beginning
parts.note: sections of writing are often indented, so their first line comes in from the margin at the start

explanation.surface: Introductory passages that appear at the start of a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Sections of prose are blocks of text whose opening line is commonly indented.

clue.text: Slippery ice, have to wrap up

indicators.note: slippery suggests sliding about, so the letters of ice and have move around

explanation.surface: Warning: the ice is slippery, so dress warmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap up a task is to complete it, and to accomplish is the same idea.

clue.text: Like a small band, able to stretch out

definitions.meaning: resembling a rubber band, the small loop that holds things together
stretchy, capable of being pulled longer and springing back

explanation.surface: A small musical group that can extend its set.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber band is made of stretchy material, and the adjective means just that ability to stretch.

clue.text: Upset hot water

definitions.meaning: to upset is to disturb or worry someone
being in hot water is the idiom for being in difficulty

explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone is to bother them, and hot water is idiomatic for a difficult situation.

clue.text: More than one construction vehicle's caught idling foully

indicators.note: caught means held inside, so the shuffled letters go within the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle, and the s completes it

indicators.note: foully means badly, so the letters of idling are rearranged

explanation.surface: Several builder's lorries left with engines running and fumes billowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foully' gives ILDING, and 'caught' means the vehicle holds it before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A construction is a built structure, and several of them are edifices or houses in the plural.

clue.text: Seems a listener's keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the musical letters sit within

parts.note: ears are what listen, so a listener's organs give ears
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: It looks as though someone listening is keeping very quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem a certain way is to look or come across that way, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Get out to absorb a politician that gets in a lather

indicators.note: absorbing means taking inside, so the politician goes into the cry

parts.note: shoo is the cry to make someone get out
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Telling a politician to leave so that someone else gets worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in a lather' sounds like getting upset, but means foams up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair-washing liquid foams up into suds, so it is something that lathers.

clue.text: Can't stand? That's typical of tailing detectives

indicators.note: tailing means following behind, so this piece comes after the detectives

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
that's like him means that's typical of him

explanation.surface: Hating something is just what you'd expect of detectives following suspects.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unable to stand something is to feel aversion to it, the verb sense of disapproval.

clue.text: Elaborate flagpole — VE Day coming up will feature it

indicators.note: in a down light coming up means the letters read from bottom to top
the words carry the letters within them, so the answer is inside

explanation.surface: A decorated flagpole will be a feature of the celebrations as VE Day approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters POLEVED sit inside 'flagpole VE Day'; 'coming up' reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate an idea is to work it out more fully, a synonym for expanding or building it out.

clue.text: Get hot when biting into humbug

indicators.note: a piece biting into another goes inside it

parts.note: rot means nonsense, as does humbug
as can mean when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: Something heats up when you bite into a mint sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: A humbug is a British boiled mint sweet, but here it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To bake in the sun is to become very warm, and the verb is used informally for getting hot.

clue.text: With different blood group, woman is surviving

indicators.note: O and A are both blood groups, so one replaces the other in the name

parts.note: Olive is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman given a transfusion of the wrong blood type still lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone still living is surviving, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Did guide distribute dive ads?

indicators.note: distribute means spread about, so the letters of dive ads are rearranged

explanation.surface: Did the tour leader hand out leaflets for scuba trips?
explanation.definitionFit: Counselled or recommended, a past-tense verb meaning gave guidance to someone.

clue.text: Peachy fried plums regularly used in turnover

indicators.note: turnover means flipped, so the chosen letters read backwards
regularly picks every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: Fried plums used in a pastry is a lovely idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks REPUS from 'fried plums'; 'used in turnover' reads it backwards. A turnover is also a folded pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Peachy is informal for excellent, so it matches the slangy word for great.

clue.text: Distinguished partners crushing opponent twice

indicators.note: crushing means squeezing on either side, so the partners surround the other letters

parts.note: in bridge South and North are partners

indicators.note: twice means the opponent appears two times

parts.note: East is an opponent of North and South at bridge

explanation.surface: A bridge pair beats a rival twice over in impressive style.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguished here is the past participle of discern, meaning made out or noticed by the eye.

clue.text: First of April, headlessly full of foolish panic

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the other letters go inside
headlessly means without its first letter, so the month loses its head
foolish suggests confusion, so the letters of panic are mixed

explanation.surface: On the first of April, a silly panic takes hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headlessly' drops the month's first letter, and 'full of' takes NCIPA, from 'foolish', before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The main or chief thing is first in importance, the adjective sense.

clue.text: Writer going to church in some European capital

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An author visits a church in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests a city, but means money; British coins are pennies, plural pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennies are British money, and the plural coins make up some of a European country's capital in the sense of funds.

clue.text: Tramp's dog's maybe rolling about

indicators.note: rolling about suggests turning over, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet, and with the s gives pets

explanation.surface: A vagrant's dog rolling around on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a vagrant but is a verb, to tread heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to tread or walk heavily, a verb synonym for a pace.

clue.text: Commander with map barking 'Retreating, no sir!' gets distinction

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of map are rearranged
retreating means going back, so the words are read backwards

explanation.surface: An officer with a map yells at a subordinate who refuses to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' makes MPA from MAP; 'Retreating' turns NO SIR into RISON.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing a distinction between things means setting them side by side to contrast them.
